verdict.rationale: Rive's docs describe components as reusable artboards with customized instances, and changes to the source component propagate to every instance, so the reusable-and-linked core is documented. Per-instance overrides are only implied by the phrase "customized instances", and variants are not mentioned anywhere in the evidence. missing for 10: documented variants, explicit per-instance override mechanics (which properties can be overridden and how overrides survive source changes), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a designer, I can build reusable components with variants and per-instance overrides that stay linked to their source

citations.quote: Components are reusable artboards. Create a component once, then use customized instances of it throughout your Rive file. Changes made to the source component are reflected across all of its instances.
Create vector graphics, responsive layouts, and reusable components
